origin: A blend of confirm and shaming. The name spread from a blog that collected cases of decline buttons worded to embarrass people.
whenToUse: You review the decline wording of popups and banners.
You explain to a team where the line against dark patterns lies.
You compare it with the honest wording on the same screen.
whenNotToUse: You want to put emotional words on a real decline button (don't).
You'd justify a metric target that doesn't respect people's choices.
You'd hide or shrink the decline option.
accessibility: Make the decline option a real button too, reachable with the keyboard.
Keep the size and contrast of both options similar.
Don't hide declining in underlined text alone.
The result sounds the same to screen readers.
